newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil panel suspends oil bill session.
newsitem.headline: Brazil panel suspends oil bill session.

text.p: A committee in Brazil's Chamber of Deputies suspended a session to debate a bill regulating the opening up of the petroleum industry because of a vote on the floor of the house on re-election, an official said.

Deputy Alberto Goldmann, the panel's president, said the committee would resume its deliberations later Tuesday or Wednesday but said a vote on the oil sector legislation would probably only take place March 4.
The bill sets down rules for private sector invetsment in the oil and gas sector. If approved, it goes to a vote on the Chamber floor and then to the Senate.
Brazil's Congress approved in 1995 the break-up of state oil firm Petrobras' monopoly but has still to pass the enabling legislation.

As prepared, the regulatory bill would allow Petrobras to maintain its rights in areas where it is already active. As a result private conmpanies are expected to go into partnership with Petrobras rather than compete against it.
The bill will also set up a regulator for the industry.
